lockedMove.speaker: William Lane Craig
lockedMove.proposition: Godless normative realism is less plausible than theism because its independently real abstract moral objects add an extravagant ontology without sufficient support.
lockedMove.sourceExcerpt: cannot overcome the presumption against platonism and hence against godless normative realism. The theist, by contrast, faces no such obstacle because he grounds moral values in a concrete object, namely God, and so is not committed to a realm of abstract objects. Thus, godless normative realism involves extravagant metaphysical claims which make it less plausible than theism
